body.content: The grounded extension's determinism comes from being the least fixed point of a monotone operator. Strengthenings that stay inside that operator family — stratification (candidate 1), anchors-as-inputs (candidate 4), edge closure (candidate 5) — preserve determinism and polynomial cost trivially, but buy discrimination at the price of changing what the fixpoint sees. Strengthenings that step outside the operator — intersection over variants (candidate 6), witness extraction with size bounds (candidate 2), acyclic-suspension refinement (candidate 3) — buy skepticism only by introducing new, un-adjudicated commitments (choice of suspect set, witness selection, the privilege of acyclic defense). The deepest unresolved question: where to draw the boundary so 'validity of every committed root' remains a property of the fixpoint rather than of an opaque post-pass.
body.possible_next_move: Formally characterize which candidate families are expressible as monotone operators over an extended state, and which require a second pass; then attack each family on its own terms.
body.unfinished: No formal operator-theoretic statement yet; the IN/OUT/UNDEC vs. suspended distinction is still informal.
body.why_keep_this: Captures the design tension all six candidates trade off, and names the meta-criterion a critic should apply to any extension proposal.
